correctness.rationale: On any periodic orbit a 1 on one shore at time t requires a 1 on the other at t-1. The resulting two-step inequalities on periodic excitation-presence flags force either no excitation, both shores every step, or strict alternation. Exact age-of-positive-state equivalence proves complete k-support in the second case and the complementary s-supports in the third. A two-step cyclic phase permutation and support parity certify least periods k and 2s, with exact surjection populations. 83 independent labelled-graph instances (1,095,764 states) and 349,504 support masks corroborate the algebraic proof; they are not substituted for it.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible full primary study (Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff, DOI:10.1214/17-AAP1350) proves a three-color synchronization criterion and asymptotic excitation rate on arbitrary graphs, not an exact all-color labelled primitive-orbit census on complete bipartite graphs. Older preprints on lattice oscillation and original model formulation do not state the finite \(K_{m,n}\) Stirling-number classification in their available material. Neighboring prior claims treat a deleted-edge graph under three-state GHM or intact bipartite graphs under cyclic successor-contact dynamics, neither implying the exact all-k result. Historical risk remains and absence from search results is not novelty proof.
residual_risks: A general three-color theorem might be algorithmically specialized to some k=3 counts, though the complete all-k population formula is not stated in its inspected main results.
Full texts of older lattice studies and the 1978 foundational article were not all inspected; an unindexed equivalent complete-bipartite specialization could exist.
No literature search establishes mathematical uniqueness; novelty is qualified to accessible evidence.

value.rationale: A natural excitable-media model on the extremal dense bipartite graph family is classified uniformly over all color counts and two unbounded shore sizes. The sharp threshold \(\min(m,n)\ge\lceil k/2\rceil\), the odd/even primitive-period bifurcation, and explicit labelled orbit census resolve a meaningful dynamical gap. The result is not just counting fixed points or a textbook substitution; it identifies constrained excitation schedules and the precise phase-surjection mechanisms behind sustained activity.
